notes: Stipendium Hungaricum is a Hungarian Government scholarship programme implemented by Tempus Public Foundation (Live check, 2026-10-14: https://stipendiumhungaricum.hu). Applicants are nominated by a Sending Partner and choose programmes through the programme's own Study Finder, which covers more than 900 study programmes at 30 Hungarian higher education institutions. No single institution, department or supervising professor is attached to the scheme; the only published contact is the Tempus Public Foundation programme contact page (https://stipendiumhungaricum.hu/contact/), not an academic supervisor. Per research rules, national government schemes with no attached institution are recorded as not_applicable.

Live check of the official NAWA page (https://nawa.gov.pl/en/students/foreign-students/the-banach-scholarship-programme/about-the-programme, 2026-10-14) confirms the Banach NAWA programme is a Polish development-aid scheme run jointly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Poland and NAWA: 'Banach NAWA programme offers scholarships for full-time second-cycle studies conducted in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education.' Applicants choose their own host university from the call announcement; no institution, department or supervising professor is attached to the scheme, and the page names no academic staff. Per research rules, national government schemes with no attached institution are recorded as not_applicable.

Live check of the official NAWA page (https://nawa.gov.pl/en/students/foreign-students/poland-my-first-choice-programme/about-the-programme, 2026-10-14) confirms the Poland My First Choice NAWA programme is a Polish government scheme: 'The Programme offers a scholarship during the statutory period of full-time second-cycle studies at academic HEIs (both public and non-public) supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education.' Live checks (2026-10-14) of https://study.gov.pl/visegrad-scholarship-programme and https://www.visegradfund.org/scholarships/ confirm the Visegrad Scholarship Programme is run by the International Visegrad Fund as a regional mobility scheme for master's and post-master's students/researchers for 1-2 semesters (1-4 semesters for In-Coming MA scholarships) at institutions across Central and Eastern Europe. study.gov.pl states 'There are various scholarship schemes available. Further information is accessible on the Visegrad Fund website'; the Fund page lists the scheme among several mobility programmes with no partner university, department or supervising professor attached. No institution-specific supervisor page exists for the scheme itself, so not_applicable.
